allResults.question: A company is building an employee policy agent. Policy documents change every week, responses must reflect the latest approved version, and users should receive citations. The base model already follows instructions adequately. Which approach should the architect recommend?
allResults.topic: D2.2 / Foundry model customization versus RAG
allResults.domainName: Agentic AI Business Solutions Architecture (Practice Quiz)
allResults.explanation: Retrieval grounding is appropriate when authoritative knowledge changes frequently and must be cited. It supplies current information at run time without changing model weights. Fine-tuning is better suited to changing behavior, style, format, or task performance.

allResults.question: A claims team has optimized its prompts, but the model still produces inconsistent JSON for numerous edge cases. The team has 2,000 reviewed prompt-response examples that demonstrate the required schema and behavior. The underlying business facts are supplied separately at run time. What is the best next step?
allResults.domainName: Agentic AI Business Solutions Architecture (Practice Quiz)
allResults.explanation: Fine-tuning is suitable when a high-quality task-specific dataset is available and the objective is more consistent behavior, formatting, or handling of many edge cases. Retrieval supplies knowledge but does not by itself train consistent schema behavior.

allResults.question: A support agent can explain return policies correctly, but it must now create a return authorization in a line-of-business system that exposes a secured API. Which extension should the architect select?
allResults.topic: D2.2 / Tools versus grounding and fine-tuning
allResults.domainName: Agentic AI Business Solutions Architecture (Practice Quiz)
allResults.explanation: Creating a record in an external system is an action with side effects, so the agent needs an authenticated tool that invokes the API. Grounding and fine-tuning do not independently provide authority or connectivity to perform the transaction.

allResults.question: A Copilot Studio agent must use a standards-based server that exposes several tools and resources. The available operations will evolve over time, and the agent should select the appropriate operation from the user's intent. Which design best meets the requirement?
allResults.topic: D2.2 / Copilot Studio MCP and generative orchestration
allResults.domainName: Agentic AI Business Solutions Architecture (Practice Quiz)
allResults.explanation: Copilot Studio can connect to an MCP server to access dynamically advertised tools and resources. MCP requires generative orchestration so the agent can select the appropriate capability.

allResults.question: An agent must enter data into a legacy desktop application. The application has no API or supported connector, and completing the process requires clicking controls and typing into visible fields. Which capability and prerequisite should the architect identify?
allResults.domainName: Agentic AI Business Solutions Architecture (Practice Quiz)
allResults.explanation: Computer Use is intended for web or desktop GUI automation when an API is unavailable. It interacts through visible controls using mouse and keyboard actions and requires generative orchestration.

allResults.question: A Computer Use agent will be shared with employees whose permissions in the target application differ by role. The organization must avoid having every execution inherit the maker's access and wants execution to stop for review when potentially harmful instructions are detected. What should the architect configure?
allResults.topic: D2.2 / Computer Use identity, security, and supervision
allResults.domainName: Agentic AI Business Solutions Architecture (Practice Quiz)
allResults.explanation: End-user credentials preserve each user's access boundary instead of running with the maker's permissions. Human supervision can stop potentially harmful instructions for review, with a configured response time limit.

allResults.question: An agent must compare several complex contract documents, reconcile conflicting clauses, and construct a defensible recommendation. Interactive latency is less important than analytical quality. Which model choice is most appropriate?
allResults.domainName: Agentic AI Business Solutions Architecture (Practice Quiz)
allResults.explanation: Reasoning models are suited to advanced problem solving and complex document comparison. They can spend additional time and reasoning tokens processing a request, so they fit when analytical quality matters more than immediate latency.

allResults.question: A company is designing a browser-based voice assistant that must listen and respond with low latency during a live conversation. Which architecture best aligns with the Microsoft Foundry Realtime API guidance?
allResults.topic: D2.2 / Realtime voice selection and limitations
allResults.domainName: Agentic AI Business Solutions Architecture (Practice Quiz)
allResults.explanation: The Realtime API supports low-latency speech-in, speech-out interaction. WebRTC is recommended for most client-side realtime audio scenarios, with a client integration terminating and relaying the user's audio stream.

allResults.question: A Copilot Studio maker publishes an agent and connects it to Teams and Microsoft 365 Copilot. The business now wants every employee to discover it in the Teams app store under Built for your org. What additional step is required?
allResults.topic: D2.2 / Teams and Microsoft 365 Copilot distribution
allResults.domainName: Agentic AI Business Solutions Architecture (Practice Quiz)
allResults.explanation: Publishing and connecting channels do not automatically place the agent in the organization-wide store. An agent intended for Built for your org must be submitted for administrator approval.

allResults.question: An Agent Builder agent in Microsoft 365 Copilot is grounded in a SharePoint site containing both general procedures and restricted legal documents. The owner enables organization-wide chat access. What should the architect expect when an employee without permission to the legal documents uses the agent?
allResults.topic: D2.2 / SharePoint grounding and permission boundaries
allResults.domainName: Agentic AI Business Solutions Architecture (Practice Quiz)
allResults.explanation: Sharing or making an agent discoverable does not grant access to its underlying SharePoint content. SharePoint and OneDrive knowledge sources continue to respect existing permissions and sensitivity labels.
